description: Linear system reachability computes sets that contain every state of `x′ = A x + B u`, when the start state is in a set `X` and the input `u(t)` can be any signal with values in a *zonotope* `U` (a center plus a list of generator vectors). Each time step of length `r` gives two sets: the *time-point* set at the end of the step, and the *time-interval* set for every moment during the step. The time-point set is `e^{Ar} X` plus the effect of the input; a truncated Taylor series gives the matrix exponential, and an interval matrix bounds the terms it cuts off. The time-interval set encloses the convex hull of `X` and its successor, plus correction terms for the curve between them. Every set is a *sound over-approximation* (it contains all true states, and possibly more), so use it to prove that a linear model stays safe, and as the inner step of nonlinear methods.

papers.title: Reachability of Uncertain Linear Systems Using Zonotopes
papers.venue: Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control (HSCC), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
